claims.title: Lapita settlement of Fiji
claims.summary: Austronesian Lapita voyagers, master navigators with distinctive pottery, reach Fiji by around 1000 BCE, founding the islands' first societies.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Fiji: Crossroads of the Pacific, from Lapita voyagers to a republic of two peoples", terralore.co/country/FJI/chronicle#ev-1000bce-lapita-settlement-of-fiji, claim TL:FJI:event:1000bce:lapita-settlement-of-fiji, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of Fijian chiefdoms
claims.summary: Fijian society develops into a hierarchy of competing chiefdoms bound by lineage, land and warfare, at the crossroads of Melanesia and Polynesia.

sources.label: Fiji — Countries (A Guide to the History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Fiji: Crossroads of the Pacific, from Lapita voyagers to a republic of two peoples", terralore.co/country/FJI/chronicle#ev-500bce-rise-of-fijian-chiefdoms, claim TL:FJI:event:500bce:rise-of-fijian-chiefdoms, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Abel Tasman sights Fiji
claims.summary: The Dutch navigator Abel Tasman becomes the first European to sight the Fijian islands, without landing among them.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Fiji: Crossroads of the Pacific, from Lapita voyagers to a republic of two peoples", terralore.co/country/FJI/chronicle#ev-1643-abel-tasman-sights-fiji, claim TL:FJI:event:1643:abel-tasman-sights-fiji, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bligh charts Fijian waters
claims.summary: Cast adrift after the Bounty mutiny, Captain William Bligh navigates his open boat between Fiji's main islands, through what is now Bligh Water.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Fiji: Crossroads of the Pacific, from Lapita voyagers to a republic of two peoples", terralore.co/country/FJI/chronicle#ev-1789-bligh-charts-fijian-waters, claim TL:FJI:event:1789:bligh-charts-fijian-waters, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sandalwood and bêche-de-mer trades
claims.summary: A sandalwood rush at Bua Bay, then the bêche-de-mer trade with China, draw traders, missionaries and muskets that reshape chiefly power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Fiji: Crossroads of the Pacific, from Lapita voyagers to a republic of two peoples", terralore.co/country/FJI/chronicle#ev-1804-sandalwood-and-beche-de-mer-trades, claim TL:FJI:event:1804:sandalwood-and-beche-de-mer-trades, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cakobau converts to Christianity
claims.summary: Seru Epenisa Cakobau, paramount chief of Bau and self-styled Tui Viti, accepts Christianity, bringing many Fijians under Methodist influence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Fiji: Crossroads of the Pacific, from Lapita voyagers to a republic of two peoples", terralore.co/country/FJI/chronicle#ev-1854-cakobau-converts-to-christianity, claim TL:FJI:event:1854:cakobau-converts-to-christianity, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Deed of Cession to Britain
claims.summary: Cakobau and other chiefs cede Fiji to Queen Victoria at Levuka, which becomes the first colonial capital of the new Crown colony.

sources.label: Levuka Historical Port Town (World Heritage List)
Fiji — Countries (A Guide to the History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Measles epidemic devastates Fiji
claims.summary: A measles epidemic with no prior immunity kills roughly a quarter of the Fijian population, striking the chiefly class especially hard.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Fiji: Crossroads of the Pacific, from Lapita voyagers to a republic of two peoples", terralore.co/country/FJI/chronicle#ev-1875-measles-epidemic-devastates-fiji, claim TL:FJI:event:1875:measles-epidemic-devastates-fiji, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Arrival of the Leonidas — first girmitiyas
claims.summary: The first ship of indentured Indian labourers reaches Fiji, beginning a system that brings over 60,000 girmitiyas to the sugar plantations.

sources.label: The historical significance of Ratu Sir Lala Sukuna

claims.title: Capital moves to Suva
claims.summary: The colonial capital is relocated from Levuka on Ovalau to Suva on Viti Levu, the larger harbour that remains Fiji's capital.

sources.label: Levuka Historical Port Town (World Heritage List)

claims.title: Native Land Trust Board established
claims.summary: Ratu Sir Lala Sukuna helps create the board that entrenches indigenous control of most Fijian land, shaping the colony's economy and politics.

sources.label: The historical significance of Ratu Sir Lala Sukuna

claims.summary: Fiji becomes independent within the Commonwealth under a power-sharing constitution, with Ratu Sir Kamisese Mara as first prime minister.

claims.title: Rabuka's coups; Fiji becomes a republic
claims.summary: Lieutenant Colonel Sitiveni Rabuka leads two military coups to assert indigenous Fijian control, ending the monarchy and declaring a republic.

claims.title: First Indo-Fijian prime minister
claims.summary: Mahendra Chaudhry, leader of the Fiji Labour Party, becomes the country's first Indo-Fijian prime minister after a landslide election.

claims.summary: Armed men led by George Speight seize parliament and hold the Chaudhry government hostage for 56 days, triggering a constitutional crisis.

claims.title: Bainimarama's coup
claims.summary: Commodore Frank Bainimarama overthrows the Qarase government in Fiji's fourth coup, beginning an extended period of military-led rule.

claims.title: New constitution adopted
claims.summary: Fiji promulgates a 2013 constitution that abolishes ethnic communal voting in favour of a single common electoral roll.

claims.title: Fiji presides over COP23
claims.summary: Fiji becomes the first small-island developing state to lead a UN climate conference, promoting the Talanoa Dialogue and the 1.5°C target.

claims.summary: Bainimarama's party loses its majority; a coalition led by Sitiveni Rabuka takes power through the ballot box, ending 16 years of his rule.
